title: Why it files some and asks about others
description: The trust model for a new user: ScanFinder auto-files the documents it's confident about and only holds the uncertain ones for Review. Explains the coloured confidence edge on queue rows, the plain-language 'why this needs review' summary, the green/amber/red field badges, and why clean documents from a trusted sender never appear here. Assumes documents are waiting in Review after the import video (Ironbridge, an untaught sender).

steps.narration: ScanFinder files the documents it's confident about by itself, and only asks you about the ones it's unsure of. Here's how to tell the difference at a glance.
steps.caption: Why it files some and asks about others

steps.narration: Everything waiting for a look sits here. The coloured edge on a document is how sure ScanFinder is: a calm edge means it's nearly there, amber means please double-check, and red means it really needs your eyes.
steps.caption: The coloured edge = how sure it is

steps.narration: At the top it tells you, in plain words, why it stopped. No jargon — just the one thing it wants you to check before it files.
steps.caption: It tells you WHY, in plain words

steps.narration: Each detail carries a little badge. Green means it's confident, amber means give it a glance, and red means check it against the page. You only ever need to look where it's actually asking.
steps.caption: Green confident · amber glance · red check

steps.narration: So what about the documents that didn't land here? Those read cleanly from a sender ScanFinder already trusts, so it filed them for you without asking. The more you confirm a sender, the more it quietly handles on its own.
steps.caption: Clean read + trusted sender = filed for you

steps.narration: So the colour tells you how sure it is, and only the uncertain ones ever need you. Next, let's see exactly where a filed document ends up.
steps.caption: Next: where your documents go
